jobs.title: Senior Manager European Initiatives

titleByLocale.fr: Directeur principal Initiatives européennes

jobs.description:
The University of Zurich, Switzerland's largest university, offers a range of attractive positions in various subject areas and professional fields. With around 10,000 employees and currently 12 professional apprenticeship streams the University offers an inspiring working environment on cutting-edge research and top-class education. Put your talent and skills to work with us. Find out more about UZH as an employer!

Aufgaben:
In this role, you will coordinate and shape UZH's partnership and network activities with European partner universities. This includes our main European networks Una Europa and LERU, but also our bilateral partnerships, working closely with colleagues across UZH, our university leadership and European partners.

Your key responsibilities include:

Una Europa:
• Coordinate UZH's engagement in Una Europa, ensuring alignment with university priorities and acting as the central point of contact for the alliance.

• Manage relationships with key stakeholders across UZH, Una Europa partner universities, the Una Europa Secretariat, Movetia and other relevant partners.

• Brief and support university leadership involved in Una Europa governance, represent UZH in relevant meetings, and implement or coordinate the follow-up of decisions.

• Oversee the implementation of Una Europa projects at UZH, including project coordination, budget management, controlling and reporting.

• Line Management of the Senior Project Lead for the main Una Europa Erasmus+ Project.

LERU & European developments:
• Represent UZH in the LERU Senior Officers Network (SON) together with the Head of Global Affairs, coordinating internal activities, consultation processes and information exchanges.

• Monitor relevant European higher education and research policy developments, where relevant, and share relevant insights within UZH and Global Affairs.

European partnerships
• Manage relationships with priority European partner universities.

• Plan and coordinate strategic partnership visits, governance meetings and events, including briefing materials, budget oversight and quality assurance.

• Coordinate partnership requests and ensure effective information management and communication around European partnership activities.

• Contribute to the implementation of UZH's Global Strategy 2030 within the European partnerships portfolio.

Anforderungen:
You are an experienced and internationally minded higher education professional with a genuine passion for European collaboration. You are energized by bringing people, institutions and ideas together and enjoy working in complex international environments where relationships, trust and long-term engagement matter.

You have a strong interest in European higher education, research and innovation, and are motivated by the opportunity to advance partnership and collaborative initiatives across Europe. Whether working on university alliances, institutional partnerships, European policy developments, you combine tactical thinking with a hands-on approach and a strong commitment to delivery.

Ideally, you bring:
• several years of professional experience in international relations, partnership development, programme management or a comparable role within higher education or a related international environment with a strong focus on Europe.

• a strong understanding of the European higher education and research landscape and a genuine interest in current developments and policy discussions across Europe.

• excellent project management and coordination skills and confidence in representing institutional interests in national and international settings.

• excellent English language skills, additional European languages are considered an asset.

Personally, you are enthusiastic, collaborative and open-minded. You enjoy working across organizational and cultural boundaries, build trusted relationships with ease and are comfortable navigating complexity and ambiguity. You combine initiative with sound judgment, are curious about new developments, and contribute actively to a supportive and collegial team environment.

Our employees benefit from a wide range of attractive offers. Find out more: https://www.uzh.ch/de/explore/work.html.

• Gestione della linea del progetto senior Lead for the main Una Europa Erasmus+ Progetto.

LERU & sviluppi europei:
• Rappresentare UZH nella rete di alti funzionari LERU (SON) insieme al capo degli affari globali, coordinando le attività interne, i processi di consultazione e gli scambi di informazioni.

• Monitorare gli sviluppi rilevanti della politica europea dell'istruzione superiore e della ricerca, ove pertinenti, e condividere approfondimenti pertinenti all'interno di UZH e Global Affairs.

Partenariati europei
• Gestire i rapporti con le università partner europee prioritarie.

• Pianificare e coordinare le visite strategiche di partenariato, incontri di governance ed eventi, compresi i materiali di briefing, la supervisione di bilancio e la garanzia di qualità.

• Coordinare le richieste di partenariato e garantire una gestione efficace delle informazioni e della comunicazione sulle attività di partenariato europeo.

• Contribuisci all'implementazione della Strategia Globale UZH 2030 all'interno del portafoglio di partnership europee.

Anforderungen:
Sei un professionista di istruzione superiore esperto e di fama internazionale con una vera passione per la collaborazione europea. Siete stimolati dal riunire persone, istituzioni e idee e godere di lavorare in ambienti internazionali complessi in cui le relazioni, la fiducia e l'impegno a lungo termine.

Hai un forte interesse per l'istruzione superiore europea, la ricerca e l'innovazione, e sono motivati dall'opportunità di promuovere partnership e iniziative collaborative in tutta Europa. Sia che lavorino su alleanze universitarie, partnership istituzionali, sviluppi politici europei, si combina il pensiero tattico con un approccio pratico e un forte impegno per la consegna.

Idealmente, si porta:
• diversi anni di esperienza professionale nelle relazioni internazionali, sviluppo di partnership, gestione di programmi o un ruolo paragonabile all'interno dell'istruzione superiore o un ambiente internazionale correlato con un forte focus sull'Europa.

• una forte comprensione del panorama europeo dell'istruzione superiore e della ricerca e un autentico interesse per gli sviluppi attuali e le discussioni politiche in tutta Europa.

• eccellenti capacità di gestione e coordinamento del progetto e fiducia nel rappresentare gli interessi istituzionali in contesti nazionali e internazionali.

• eccellenti competenze linguistiche, lingue europee aggiuntive sono considerate un bene.

Personalmente, sei entusiasta, collaborativo e di mentalità aperta. Ti piace lavorare attraverso confini organizzativi e culturali, costruire relazioni fidate con facilità e sono confortevoli navigare complessità e ambiguità. Unisci l'iniziativa al giudizio sonoro, sei curioso di nuovi sviluppi e contribuisci attivamente a un ambiente di team di supporto e collegiale.

• Beaufsichtigen Sie die Umsetzung von Una Europa Projekten an der UZH, einschließlich Projektkoordination, Budgetmanagement, Controlling und Reporting.

• Leitungsmanagement des Senior Project Lead für die Haupt Una Europa Erasmus+ Projekt.

LERU & europäische Entwicklungen:
• Vertretung der UZH im LERU Senior Officers Network (SON) gemeinsam mit dem Head of Global Affairs, Koordination interner Aktivitäten, Beratungsprozesse und Informationsaustausch.

• Überwachung relevanter Entwicklungen der europäischen Hochschul- und Forschungspolitik, soweit relevant, und Austausch relevanter Erkenntnisse innerhalb der UZH und Global Affairs.

Europäische Partnerschaften
• Verwaltung der Beziehungen zu vorrangigen europäischen Partneruniversitäten.

• Planung und Koordinierung strategischer Partnerschaftsbesuche, Governance-Sitzungen und Veranstaltungen, einschließlich Briefing-Materialien, Haushaltsaufsicht und Qualitätssicherung.

• Koordinierung von Partnerschaftsanfragen und Gewährleistung eines effektiven Informationsmanagements und einer effektiven Kommunikation rund um europäische Partnerschaftsaktivitäten.

• Beitrag zur Umsetzung der globalen Strategie 2030 der UZH im Portfolio europäischer Partnerschaften.

Anforderungen:
Sie sind eine erfahrene und international denkende Hochschulfachkraft mit einer echten Leidenschaft für die europäische Zusammenarbeit. Sie werden angeregt, Menschen, Institutionen und Ideen zusammenzubringen und genießen es, in komplexen internationalen Umgebungen zu arbeiten, in denen Beziehungen, Vertrauen und langfristiges Engagement wichtig sind.

Sie haben ein starkes Interesse an europäischer Hochschulbildung, Forschung und Innovation und sind motiviert durch die Möglichkeit, Partnerschaften und Kooperationsinitiativen in ganz Europa voranzutreiben. Ob Sie an Hochschulallianzen, institutionellen Partnerschaften, europapolitischen Entwicklungen arbeiten, Sie kombinieren taktisches Denken mit einem praktischen Ansatz und einem starken Engagement für die Umsetzung.

Idealerweise bringen Sie:
• mehrjährige Berufserfahrung in internationalen Beziehungen, Partnerschaftsentwicklung, Programmmanagement oder einer vergleichbaren Rolle in der Hochschulbildung oder einem damit verbundenen internationalen Umfeld mit einem starken Fokus auf Europa.

• ein starkes Verständnis der europäischen Hochschul- und Forschungslandschaft und ein echtes Interesse an aktuellen Entwicklungen und politischen Diskussionen in ganz Europa.

• ausgezeichnete Projektmanagement- und Koordinationsfähigkeiten und Vertrauen in die Vertretung institutioneller Interessen im nationalen und internationalen Umfeld.

• hervorragende Englischkenntnisse, zusätzliche europäische Sprachen gelten als Aktivposten.

Persönlich sind Sie enthusiastisch, kooperativ und aufgeschlossen. Sie arbeiten gerne über organisatorische und kulturelle Grenzen hinweg, bauen mit Leichtigkeit vertrauenswürdige Beziehungen auf und navigieren bequem durch Komplexität und Mehrdeutigkeit. Sie verbinden Initiative mit fundiertem Urteilsvermögen, sind neugierig auf neue Entwicklungen und tragen aktiv zu einem unterstützenden und kollegialen Teamumfeld bei.

Mettez votre talent et vos compétences au travail avec nous. En savoir plus sur UZH en tant qu'employeur!

Aufgaben:
Dans ce rôle, vous coordonnerez et façonnerez les activités de partenariat et de réseau de l'UZH avec les universités partenaires européennes. Cela inclut nos principaux réseaux européens Una Europa et LERU, mais aussi nos partenariats bilatéraux, en étroite collaboration avec nos collègues de l'UEH, notre leadership universitaire et nos partenaires européens.

Vos principales responsabilités comprennent :

Una Europa:
• Coordonner l'engagement de l'UZH à Una Europa, en assurant l'alignement sur les priorités universitaires et en agissant comme point de contact central pour l'alliance.

• Gérer les relations avec les principales parties prenantes dans les universités partenaires d'UZH, Una Europa, le Secrétariat d'Una Europa, Movtia et d'autres partenaires concernés.

• Brièvement et soutenir le leadership universitaire impliqué dans la gouvernance d'Una Europa, représenter l'UZH dans les réunions pertinentes, et mettre en œuvre ou coordonner le suivi des décisions.

• Superviser la mise en œuvre des projets Una Europa à l'UZH, y compris la coordination des projets, la gestion budgétaire, le contrôle et l'établissement de rapports.

• Gestion de ligne du chef de projet principal pour la principale Una Europa Erasmus+ Projet.

LERU & Développements européens:
• Représenter l'UZH au Réseau des officiers supérieurs (SON) de LERU en collaboration avec le chef des affaires mondiales, en coordonnant les activités internes, les processus de consultation et les échanges d'informations.

• Suivre l'évolution de la politique européenne en matière d'enseignement supérieur et de recherche, le cas échéant, et partager les informations pertinentes au sein de l'UEH et des Affaires mondiales.

Partenariats européens
• Gérer les relations avec les universités partenaires européennes prioritaires.

• Planifier et coordonner les visites en partenariat stratégique, les réunions et les événements sur la gouvernance, y compris les documents d'information, le contrôle budgétaire et l'assurance de la qualité.

• Coordonner les demandes de partenariat et assurer une gestion et une communication efficaces de l'information dans le cadre des activités de partenariat européen.

• Contribuer à la mise en œuvre de la Stratégie mondiale 2030 de l'UZH au sein du portefeuille de partenariats européens.

- C'est pas vrai.
Vous êtes un professionnel de l'enseignement supérieur expérimenté et international avec une véritable passion pour la collaboration européenne. Vous êtes énergisé en réunissant des gens, des institutions et des idées et vous aimez travailler dans des environnements internationaux complexes où les relations, la confiance et l'engagement à long terme comptent.

Vous vous intéressez vivement à l'enseignement supérieur, à la recherche et à l'innovation en Europe, et vous êtes motivés par l'occasion de faire progresser les partenariats et les initiatives de collaboration dans toute l'Europe. Que vous travailliez sur les alliances universitaires, les partenariats institutionnels, l'évolution de la politique européenne, vous combinez la pensée tactique avec une approche pratique et un engagement ferme en matière d'exécution.

Idéalement, vous apportez:
• plusieurs années d'expérience professionnelle dans les relations internationales, le développement de partenariats, la gestion de programmes ou un rôle comparable au sein de l'enseignement supérieur ou d'un environnement international connexe, l'accent étant mis sur l'Europe.

• une bonne compréhension du paysage européen de l'enseignement supérieur et de la recherche et un véritable intérêt pour les développements actuels et les discussions politiques dans toute l'Europe.

• d'excellentes compétences en matière de gestion et de coordination de projets et la confiance dans la représentation des intérêts institutionnels dans les contextes national et international.

• d'excellentes compétences en anglais, d'autres langues européennes sont considérées comme un atout.

Personnellement, vous êtes enthousiaste, collaboratif et ouvert d'esprit. Vous aimez travailler au-delà des frontières organisationnelles et culturelles, établir des relations de confiance avec facilité et sont confortables naviguer la complexité et l'ambiguïté. Vous combinez initiative et bon jugement, vous êtes curieux de nouveaux développements et vous contribuez activement à un environnement d'équipe solidaire et collégial.

• Intellektuelle Neugierde und ausgeprägte Freude an Forschung und Lehre.

jobs.description:
The University of Zurich, Switzerland's largest university, offers a range of attractive positions in various subject areas and professional fields. With around 10,000 employees and currently 12 professional apprenticeship streams the University offers an inspiring working environment on cutting-edge research and top-class education. Put your talent and skills to work with us. Find out more about UZH as an employer!

Aufgaben:
Grasslands are highly diverse ecosystems that provide important ecosystem functions. Maintaining or restoring grassland biodiversity increases their ability to deal with environmental disturbances such as fires and droughts, which are expected to increase in frequency and severity in the coming century. However, our understanding of the mechanisms creating and maintaining the high species diversity in grasslands remain poorly understood, impeding the design of successful management strategies. An increasing body of evidence suggests, however, that interactions between plants and the community of soil organisms create plant-soil feedbacks that play a crucial role in creating and maintaining grassland biodiversity.
A new collaborative project between the University of Zurich and the University of Kansas (USA) aims to advance our understanding of how plant-soil feedbacks contribute to the functioning of grassland ecosystems. The research team in Zurich (consisting of 2 PhD students, an outreach coordinator and the PI) will develop and analyze mathematical models that quantify the interactions between plant and soil communities. These models will be calibrated and validated with the results of greenhouse experiments and long-term field experiments conducted with north American grassland species. The project aims to improve our fundamental understanding of grassland ecosystem functioning, which can then be used in conservation, restoration and education in the USA and Switzerland.
We invite candidates to apply for (one of) the two positions listed below:

PhD Position 1: Theory and tests of plant-soil feedback: implications for long-term dynamics
Your tasks:
1) Develop a model-data integration framework: Using data from many experiments with two North Carolina grassland species, you will develop and validate a mathematical model that describes how the soil community builds up over time, and how these soil dynamics affect the two plant species.
2) Extend this framework to multiple species: Using data from experiments that will be conducted with six Kansas grassland species, and recent theoretical advances to describe community-level plant-soil feedbacks, you will extend the applicability of the framework to more than two species.
3) Integrate findings with community-level models of plant-soil feedback: You will integrate the framework with the findings of the other PhD student project, which focuses on describing the consequences of plant-soil feedback on plant community dynamics.

PhD Position 2: Theory and tests of plant-soil feedback: implications for plant community dynamics
Your tasks:
1) Model the benefits of plant community diversity for ecosystem functioning: Using data from a long-term biodiversity field experiment, you will parameterize a model in which plant community dynamics are structured by plant-soil feedbacks. Model analysis will focus on how plant community diversity is created and maintained by plant-soil feedback, and how this affects ecosystem functions such as productivity.
2) Model impacts of dispersal limitation on biodiversity and ecosystem function: You will study to what extent previously unexplained trends in the experimental data can be modelled by incorporation of dispersal constraints and their impact on plant-soil community interactions and plant competition.
3) Integrate findings with dynamical soil community models of plant-soil feedback: You will integrate the multi-species model framework that includes dispersal constraints with the findings of the other PhD student project, which focuses on describing the consequences of plant-soil feedback on long-term dynamics.

For both PhD positions, the findings of each of the three tasks are expected to be reported in three scientific articles. These articles will then form the basis of the PhD thesis, and an education module for Swiss and American high school students, which will be developed by the PIs and the project's outreach coordinator.

Anforderungen:
• Enthusiastic about discovering new explanations for real-world ecological phenomena through mathematical model development, analytical analyses and simulations.

• A Masters of Science (MSc) or equivalent degree from an accredited academic institution, in Environmental & Earth System Science, Geo- & Environmental Physics, Computational & Mathematical Biology, Ecology & Evolution, or related fields.

• Experience in developing and analysing ecosystem models, using (symbolic) coding languages such as MATLAB, Python, Fortran, Julia, Mathematica and/or R.

• Experience with statistical data analysis using open and reproducible methods

• Motivated to collaborate with project team members including field ecologists, and to participate in ecological experiments and field data collection.

Wir bieten:
Our employees benefit from a wide range of attractive offers. Find out more: https://www.uzh.ch/de/explore/work.html.

3) Integrate findings with community-level models of plant-soil feedback: You will integrate the framework with the findings of the other PhD student project, which focuses on describing the consequences of plant-soil feedback on plant community dynamics.

PhD Position 2: Theory and tests of plant-soil feedback: implications for plant community dynamics
Your tasks:
1) Model the benefits of plant community diversity for ecosystem functioning: Using data from a long-term biodiversity field experiment, you will parameterize a model in which plant community dynamics are structured by plant-soil feedbacks. Model analysis will focus on how plant community diversity is created and maintained by plant-soil feedback, and how this affects ecosystem functions such as productivity.
2) Model impacts of dispersal limitation on biodiversity and ecosystem function: You will study to what extent previously unexplained trends in the experimental data can be modelled by incorporation of dispersal constraints and their impact on plant-soil community interactions and plant competition.
3) Integrate findings with dynamical soil community models of plant-soil feedback: You will integrate the multi-species model framework that includes dispersal constraints with the findings of the other PhD student project, which focuses on describing the consequences of plant-soil feedback on long-term dynamics.

For both PhD positions, the findings of each of the three tasks are expected to be reported in three scientific articles. These articles will then form the basis of the PhD thesis, and an education module for Swiss and American high school students, which will be developed by the PIs and the project's outreach coordinator.

Anforderungen:
• Enthusiastic about discovering new explanations for real-world ecological phenomena through mathematical model development, analytical analyses and simulations.

• A Masters of Science (MSc) or equivalent degree from an accredited academic institution, in Environmental & Earth System Science, Geo- & Environmental Physics, Computational & Mathematical Biology, Ecology & Evolution, or related fields.

• Experience in developing and analysing ecosystem models, using (symbolic) coding languages such as MATLAB, Python, Fortran, Julia, Mathematica and/or R.

• Experience with statistical data analysis using open and reproducible methods

• Motivated to collaborate with project team members including field ecologists, and to participate in ecological experiments and field data collection.

jobs.description:
The University of Zurich, Switzerland's largest university, offers a range of attractive positions in various subject areas and professional fields. With around 10,000 employees and currently 12 professional apprenticeship streams the University offers an inspiring working environment on cutting-edge research and top-class education. Put your talent and skills to work with us. Find out more about UZH as an employer!

Aufgaben:
1. Analysing how participants' definitions of art change before and after their dialogue with the AI chatbot;
2. Coding learner–AI dialogues using a novel coding framework, for which training will be provided; and
3. Identifying and interpreting relevant linguistic, communicative, and dialogic features in the dialogues.

A computer program will be developed to automate parts of the analysis. An important part of your work will therefore be to verify the quality of the automated coding and help identify cases in which human interpreta-tion remains necessary.

Anforderungen:
• Excellent command of English and German;

• The ability to interpret language and support conclusions with evidence from the text; and

• Previous experience with qualitative content analysis, dialogue analysis, discourse analysis, or linguistic coding-or a willingness to learn and gain experience in these methods.
 Knowledge of additional Swiss national languages is an advantage.

Advantageous but non-essential requirements:
• Familiarity with R, Python, SPSS, or similar tools;

• An interest in generative AI and learner–AI interaction; and

• An interest in art and in the question of what may-or may not-count as art

• Collaboration in interdisciplinary research projects

Anforderungen:

jobs.description:
The University of Zurich, Switzerland's largest university, offers a range of attractive positions in various subject areas and professional fields. With around 10,000 employees and currently 12 professional apprenticeship streams the University offers an inspiring working environment on cutting-edge research and top-class education. Put your talent and skills to work with us. Find out more about UZH as an employer!

Aufgaben:
The incoming Assistant Professor is expected to dive deep, charting unexplored territories in virology and/or host-pathogen interactions. Ideally the researcher shows a clinical interest – a physician scientist with training in infectious diseases would be very welcome. We are searching for a visionary - someone keen on doing experimental work and/or translational science. A passion for teaching, paired with the leadership skills required to lead a research team, is indispensable.

Anforderungen:
We seek excellence.
• Candidates must satisfy the eligibility criteria for SNSF starting grants ( SNSF Starting Grants ), ERC consolidator grants ( Consolidator Grant|ERC ), or the Professor Dr Max Cloëtta Foundation ( Medical Research Position - Professor Dr Max Cloëtta Foundation ).

• We expect candidates to stand out with research outputs that not only exceed their doctoral contributions but also redefine boundaries in the field.

We are particularly interested in the following expertise:
• biology of viruses

• immunopathology caused by viruses

• immune responses to viruses

• novel treatment strategies to fight viruses

• novel vaccination strategies

• data science in virology

We seek an ambitious investigator developing an internationally competitive research program addressing fundamental or translational questions in virology. While research on clinically relevant viral pathogens is particularly encouraged, outstanding candidates working on any aspect of virus biology or virus–host interactions are warmly invited to apply.

Wir bieten:
Our employees benefit from a wide range of attractive offers. Find out more: https://www.uzh.ch/de/explore/work.html.

titleByLocale.it: Postdoc in Economics of Education and Labor Economics
titleByLocale.en: Postdoc in Economics of Education and Labor Economics
titleByLocale.de: Postdoc in Economics of Education and Labor Economics
titleByLocale.fr: Postdoc in Economics of Education and Labor Economics

jobs.description:
The University of Zurich, Switzerland's largest university, offers a range of attractive positions in various subject areas and professional fields. With around 10,000 employees and currently 12 professional apprenticeship streams the University offers an inspiring working environment on cutting-edge research and top-class education. Put your talent and skills to work with us. Find out more about UZH as an employer!

Aufgaben:
The successful candidate will:
• develop and publish research projects in economics of education, labor/personnel economics, and applied mi-croeconomics

• take a central role in field experiments, from research design and partner coordination to data collection and analysiss

• work with experimental, survey, and administrative data and contribute to research papers, presentations, grant-related outputs, and policy-oriented communication

• collaborate closely with doctoral students, research assistants, and external partners

• contribute to teaching and administrative duties, which are expected to remain limited to approximately 20% of the position on average, with the remaining time devoted to research

The position is for three years, with the possibility of extension for another three years upon mutual agreement. The start date is flexible. The earliest possible start date is November 1, 2026, but a later start date until summer 2027 is possible.

Anforderungen:
Candidates should hold, by the start date, a PhD in economics or a closely related field.
Candidates should have:
• strong training in applied microeconomics, econometrics, and causal inference

• a strong research interest in economics of education, labor economics, personnel economics, or related applied-micro fields

• prior experience with field-based or experimental empirical research, such as field experiments, survey experiments, or empirical projects involving external partners

• excellent oral and written communication skills in English

• the ability to work independently, reliably, and with strong attention to detail

• a collaborative working style and interest in contributing actively to a research team

• German skills at B1 level or higher, explicitly stated in the CV. In exceptional cases, French skills at B2 level or higher may substitute for German skills; applications that do not state the relevant German or French profi-ciency level will not be considered. These language skills are relevant for fieldwork and collaboration with field partners and policy institutions.

We offer a friendly, research-oriented academic environment in a team that works closely together. The position provides strong support for academic development, including room to develop independent and joint research projects, close involvement in ongoing empirical projects, and support for presenting research at international conferences. Diversity and inclusion are important to us.
Salary is in accordance with the salary guidelines of the Canton of Zurich.
International candidates are welcome. For the successful candidate, the University of Zurich will support and coordinate the work-permit process in accordance with Swiss regulations.
The place of work is Plattenstrasse 14, 8032 Zurich. The team works primarily in person in Zurich; limited remote work is possible by arrangement.

Wir bieten:

The University of Zurich, Switzerland's largest university, offers a range of attractive positions in various subject areas and professional fields. With around 10,000 employees and currently 12 professional apprenticeship streams the University offers an inspiring working environment on cutting-edge research and top-class education. Put your talent and skills to work with us. Find out more about UZH as an employer!

Aufgaben:
In collaboration with a team from the NCCR Work Package “Events” and under the supervision of Professor Balthasar Bickel, the postdoc will lead and develop a series of studies using chiefly experimental methods to investigate language processing and planning and the wider cognitive background of this in a diverse set of languages, drawing chiefly on the NCCR's existing network of collaborations worldwide ( NCCR research facilities ). Place of work is Zurich, Switzerland, but the successful candidate is expected to conduct experiments in various places across the world.

Anforderungen:
Successful candidates will be thoroughly familiar with experimental methods and statistical data analysis in language science. They are trained in psycholinguistics, neurolinguistics, and/or linguistics and are keen on engaging with evolutionary questions. Experience with cross-cultural fieldwork is an additional strong asset.

The NCCR Evolving Language places great emphasis on teamwork and multidisciplinary perspectives. Strong communication and collaboration skills are essential. Excellent oral and written communication in English is required.

Wir bieten:
Our employees benefit from a wide range of attractive offers. Find out more: https://www.uzh.ch/de/explore/work.html.

jobs.title: Biomedizinische:r Analytiker:in

titleByLocale.fr: Biomedizinische:r Analytiker:in

jobs.description:
Als grösste Universität der Schweiz bietet die Universität Zürich eine Vielzahl von attraktiven Positionen in verschiedenen Fachbereichen und Berufsfeldern. Mit rund 10'000 Mitarbeitenden und aktuell 12 Berufsprofilen für Lernende bietet die Universität ein inspirierendes Arbeitsumfeld in der Spitzenforschung und Bildung. Setzen Sie Ihr Talent und Ihre Fähigkeiten bei uns ein. Erfahren Sie mehr über die UZH als Arbeitgeberin!

Aufgaben:
• Klassische Routinetätigkeiten im Histologielabor (Histotechnik inkl. Gefriertechnik und Spezialfärbungen; Zytologie; Digitalisierung von Schnitten)
• Übernahme weiterer Tätigkeiten in zusätzlichen Bereichen wie Immunhistochemie, Molekularbiologie (PCR, qRT-PCR, ISH), ELISA, Immunoblotting, Transmissionselektronenmikroskopie, Aufarbeitung von Labortierproben
• Etablierung neuer Protokolle auf der Basis etablierter Methoden
• Labor-spezifische Aufgaben im Rahmen des Qualitätsmanagements des IVPZ (ISO/IEC 17025; STS 255)

Anforderungen:
• Abgeschlossene Ausbildung als BMA, MTLA, Biologielaborant:in oder vergleichbar, mit Erfahrung in der Histologie
• Interesse am Erlernen von neuen Techniken, rasche Auffassungsgabe, Flexibilität, zuverlässige und exakte Arbeitsweise
• Teamgeist, gepaart mit Freude am selbständigen Arbeiten
• Gute mündliche und schriftliche Deutschkenntnisse, Englischkenntnisse sind von Vorteil
• Anwendungssicherheit in Windows-Office

Unsere Mitarbeitenden profitieren von vielfältigen und attraktiven Angeboten. Erfahre mehr unter: https://www.uzh.ch/de/explore/work.html.

jobs.title: Identity & Access Management Engineer (IAM)

titleByLocale.fr: Identity & Access Management Ingénieur (IAM)

jobs.description:
Als grösste Universität der Schweiz bietet die Universität Zürich eine Vielzahl von attraktiven Positionen in verschiedenen Fachbereichen und Berufsfeldern. Mit rund 10'000 Mitarbeitenden und aktuell 12 Berufsprofilen für Lernende bietet die Universität ein inspirierendes Arbeitsumfeld in der Spitzenforschung und Bildung. Setzen Sie Ihr Talent und Ihre Fähigkeiten bei uns ein. Erfahren Sie mehr über die UZH als Arbeitgeberin!

Aufgaben:
• Betrieb der bestehenden sowie Konfiguration und Weiterentwicklung der neuen IAM-Suite

• Unterstützung der UZH Angehörigen durch Pflege der Identitäten, Zugriffe, Systeme und Schnittstellen

• Implementierung und Pflege von Prozessen, Workflows und deren Automatisierung

• Ablösung des aktuellen Systems mit Entwicklung, Aufbau und Betrieb der neuen Lösung

• Aufbau und Integration von Rollen und Applikationen in die IAM-Landschaft

• Verantwortung für den durchgängigen Betrieb inkl. Lifecycle-Management

Anforderungen:
• Höhere technische Ausbildung in Informatik oder vergleichbare Aus-/Weiterbildung

• Idealerweise bereits schwerpunktmässig auf Identity und Access Management spezialisiert

• Kenntnisse moderner IAM - Suiten und der damit verbundenen Aufgaben

• Bereitschaft das aktuelle System im Face-out zu begleiten

• Kenntnisse in der Rollenentwicklung von Vorteil

• Kenntnisse im Thema Automatisierung und AI von Vorteil

• Verständnis der End-zu-End Prozesse im IAM sind wichtig

• Sie sind eine engagierte Persönlichkeit, schätzen kollegiales Teamwork

• Hohes Engagement, Eigenverantwortung und Selbstständigkeit

• Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse und gute Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift

• Hohe Lernbereitschaft und Affinität zur Gestaltung neuer IT-Umgebungen

Mit rund 10'000 Mitarbeitenden und aktuell 12 Berufsprofilen für Lernende bietet die Universität ein inspirierendes Arbeitsumfeld in der Spitzenforschung und Bildung. Setzen Sie Ihr Talent und Ihre Fähigkeiten bei uns ein. Erfahren Sie mehr über die UZH als Arbeitgeberin!

Aufgaben:
• Betrieb der bestehenden sowie Konfiguration und Weiterentwicklung der neuen IAM-Suite

• Unterstützung der UZH Angehörigen durch Pflege der Identitäten, Zugriffe, Systeme und Schnittstellen

• Implementierung und Pflege von Prozessen, Workflows und deren Automatisierung

• Ablösung des aktuellen Systems mit Entwicklung, Aufbau und Betrieb der neuen Lösung

• Aufbau und Integration von Rollen und Applikationen in die IAM-Landschaft

• Verantwortung für den durchgängigen Betrieb inkl. Lifecycle-Management

Anforderungen:
• Höhere technische Ausbildung in Informatik oder vergleichbare Aus-/Weiterbildung

• Idealerweise bereits schwerpunktmässig auf Identity und Access Management spezialisiert

• Kenntnisse moderner IAM - Suiten und der damit verbundenen Aufgaben

• Bereitschaft das aktuelle System im Face-out zu begleiten

• Kenntnisse in der Rollenentwicklung von Vorteil

• Kenntnisse im Thema Automatisierung und AI von Vorteil

• Verständnis der End-zu-End Prozesse im IAM sind wichtig

• Sie sind eine engagierte Persönlichkeit, schätzen kollegiales Teamwork

• Hohes Engagement, Eigenverantwortung und Selbstständigkeit

• Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse und gute Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift

• Hohe Lernbereitschaft und Affinität zur Gestaltung neuer IT-Umgebungen

titleByLocale.fr: PhD position – Pastoralist Futures: Land Transformation in East Africa's Drylands

jobs.description:
The University of Zurich, Switzerland's largest university, offers a range of attractive positions in various subject areas and professional fields. With around 10,000 employees and currently 12 professional apprenticeship streams the University offers an inspiring working environment on cutting-edge research and top-class education. Put your talent and skills to work with us. Find out more about UZH as an employer!

Aufgaben:
The PhD candidate will develop a dissertation research project aligned with the project theme above and will be supervised by Dr. Asebe Regassa Debelo.

You will join the Political Geography Group, which brings together researchers from Asia, Africa, and Europe to study the entanglements of development, humanitarianism, war, displacement, extraction, frontier and border violence, and environmental change.

Alongside your PhD research, the position includes teaching responsibilities as required by the Graduate School in Geography and Earth System Sciences.

Anforderungen:
You have or are close to completing a Master's degree in human geography, anthropology, development studies, area studies, or another related discipline

In addition, research experience in East African pastoralist territories and language skills (Swahili and/or Afaan Oromo) will be an asset.

jobs.title: MSCA Doctoral Position on Balancing Individual AI-Augmentation with Organisational Stability

titleByLocale.en: MSCA Doctoral Position on Balancing Individual AI-Augmentation with Organisational Stability
titleByLocale.it: MSCA Doctoral Position on Balancing Individual AI-Augmentation with Organisational Stability
titleByLocale.de: MSCA Doctoral Position on Balancing Individual AI-Augmentation with Organisational Stability
titleByLocale.fr: MSCA Doctoral Position on Balancing Individual AI-Augmentation with Organisational Stability

jobs.description:
The University of Zurich, Switzerland's largest university, offers a range of attractive positions in various subject areas and professional fields. With around 10,000 employees and currently 12 professional apprenticeship streams the University offers an inspiring working environment on cutting-edge research and top-class education. Put your talent and skills to work with us. Find out more about UZH as an employer!

Aufgaben:
• Examine through qualitative methods how workers build personalised routines around agentic and generative AI and how these routines affect collaboration, oversight and resilience.

• Compare bottom-up experimentation and shadow AI with formal top-down rollout.

• Combine longitudinal cases, observation, digital diaries, interviews and collaboration-network analysis.

• Develop a framework and practical guidance on disclosure, versioning, audit trails, handovers and workflow portability.

• Refine the research questions and design with the supervision team and prepare ethics, data-management and open-science materials.

• Complete a doctoral thesis and related research outputs under the host doctoral programme and EMANAIRE plan.

• Take part in local and network-wide training, cohort activities, reviews, dissemination and practitioner engagement.

• Undertake the six-month intersectoral secondment and the separate academic mobility visit.

• Contribute to research integrity, equality, responsible AI, open science and FAIR data practices.

• Complete at least 20 ECTS credits of structured doctoral training, including at least 10 ECTS credits through network-wide provision. EMANAIRE combines local doctoral courses with three residential schools, monthly paper-development seminars, work-package workshops and network reviews.

A Personal Career Development Plan will be agreed within the first three months and reviewed every six months.

Anforderungen:
Applicants should hold, or be close to completing by the start date, a relevant master's degree or equivalent and demonstrate the potential to undertake independent doctoral research. Research, policy or industry experience relevant to the project is advantageous.

Project-relevant experience may include
• Interest in digital sociology, work, shadow IT or AI, organisational resilience or technology governance.

• Experience or training in qualitative research and interest in mixed-methods integration.

• Ability to examine organisational culture, power, disclosure and control with analytical sensitivity.

Language skills
Excellent English language skills, both written and spoken, are essential.

MSCA eligibility
Applicants may be of any nationality. To be eligible for MSCA funding, the selected candidate must, on the first day of MSCA employment:
(i) not hold a doctoral degree; candidates who have successfully defended a doctoral thesis but have not yet formally received the degree are not eligible;
(ii) comply with the MSCA mobility rule, meaning they must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Switzerland for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately preceding that date, excluding compulsory national service, short stays such as holidays, and time spent in a procedure for obtaining refugee status under the Geneva Convention; and
(iii) be enrolled in, or meet the conditions required for timely enrolment in, the doctoral programme leading to the degree specified in this notice. The appointment is conditional on documentary verification of these conditions and fulfilment of the host institution's doctoral admission requirements.
